notes.4: There was some confusion identifying a mitochondrion in a photomicrograph with a significant number selecting the ribosome. Candidates should be able to identify cell structures in images and drawings.
notes.7: Some incorrectly thought that decreasing the concentration gradient would increase the rate of diffusion.
notes.8: Only a few candidates could correctly interpret the osmosis experiment. Most candidates thought that the solution in the test-tube was water.
notes.9: Some candidates could not identify the correct test and positive result for reducing sugars.
notes.10: Whilst the majority of candidates could identify that protein digestion would happen fastest at the higher temperature; some did not realise that an enzyme found in the stomach would work best at a lower pH.
notes.12: Few candidates could correctly recognise the description as assimilation, many thought it was absorption.
notes.23: Many candidates thought that the bladder is where urea is excreted rather than the kidney.
notes.29: Many candidates did not know the conditions required for germination. Sunlight is not required but oxygen is required.
notes.30: Whilst most candidates correctly identified the changes in the lining of the uterus in the days before ovulation, a significant number thought that it was breaking down or thinning.
notes.33: Many candidates could correctly describe the variation in height and the reasons for this variation, some did not think that the environment affects height.
